invented_requirements: Rejecting every unknown option conflicts with both existing count-only behavior and the owner decision that option-looking single arguments other than `--uppercase` remain valid names.
Requiring flag handling and uppercase transformation to live specifically in the CLI path invents an internal implementation constraint; the owner explicitly left placement to the implementation.
failures: The contract changes `main(["--other"])` from a successful greeting to a usage error, despite the preservation request, audited repository behavior, and owner oracle requiring other option-looking single arguments to remain names.
The contract overconstrains implementation structure by assigning parsing and transformation to the CLI path when the owner oracle permits any internal placement preserving observable behavior.
summary: The interview efficiently resolved the three genuinely material observable choices, and correctly recalled uppercase scope, flag placement/repetition, reserved handling of `--uppercase`, and exact usage text/status. However, the final contract materially broadened rejection to all unknown options, contradicting the owner oracle and existing single-argument behavior, and added an unsupported internal-design constraint. It is therefore not implementation-ready as written.
